title: Hydrant Pressure Drop: Additional Attack Lines

scene.description: Engine 181 is connected to a hydrant. Use the measured flow, static pressure, and residual pressure to project available flow at a 20 PSI residual, then determine how many additional same-flow attack lines can be supported.

problems.title: Hydrant Pressure Drop: Additional Attack Lines
problems.question: Engine 181 is connected to a hydrant. Static pressure is 80 PSI. With one line flowing 185 GPM, residual pressure is 70 PSI. Project the available flow at a 20 PSI residual. How many additional 185 GPM lines can be added without exceeding that projected flow?
problems.inputLabel: How many additional lines can be added?
formulaBreakdown: Round down to 1 additional full-flow line.
problems.instructorExplanation: Hydrant available-flow projection uses the 0.54 exponent. After projecting flow at 20 PSI residual, subtract the flow already in service and divide by the flow of each additional line.
problems.explainMistake: Do not use a simple square-root relationship. The standard hydrant available-flow projection uses an exponent of 0.54.

problems.title: Hydrant Drop: 90 Static to 70 Residual
problems.question: Static pressure is 90 PSI. With one line flowing 185 GPM, residual pressure is 70 PSI. Project available flow at a 20 PSI residual. How many additional 185 GPM lines can be added without exceeding that projected flow?
problems.inputLabel: How many additional lines can be added?
formulaBreakdown: Round down to 0 additional full-flow lines.
problems.instructorExplanation: Use the 0.54 hydrant available-flow exponent, then subtract the flow already in service before determining additional full-flow lines.
problems.explainMistake: Even though the projected additional capacity is close to one more 185 GPM line, it does not fully support that line at the selected 20 PSI residual target.

problems.title: Hydrant Drop: 80 Static to 65 Residual
problems.question: Static pressure is 80 PSI. With one line flowing 185 GPM, residual pressure is 65 PSI. Project available flow at a 20 PSI residual. How many additional 185 GPM lines can be added without exceeding that projected flow?
problems.inputLabel: How many additional lines can be added?
formulaBreakdown: Round down to 1 additional full-flow line.
problems.instructorExplanation: Use the 0.54 hydrant available-flow exponent and compare the remaining projected capacity with the flow of one additional line.
problems.explainMistake: Do not replace the 0.54 exponent with 0.50; that changes the projected available GPM.

problems.title: Hydrant Drop: 80 Static to 70 Residual
problems.question: Static pressure is 80 PSI. With one line flowing 150 GPM, residual pressure is 70 PSI. Project available flow at a 20 PSI residual. How many additional 150 GPM lines can be added without exceeding that projected flow?
problems.inputLabel: How many additional lines can be added?
formulaBreakdown: Round down to 1 additional full-flow line.
problems.instructorExplanation: Use the 0.54 hydrant available-flow exponent and then calculate how many complete additional 150 GPM lines fit within the remaining projected capacity.
problems.explainMistake: The projected available GPM changes with the known test flow; use the 150 GPM value stated in this variation.
